title: FM27 Cheap Players — Where the Live Lists Are, and How to Cost a Deal
description: FM27 bargains without stale numbers: the maintainer lists that stay current, the transfer-plus-wage sum to run before calling a player cheap, and why a low fee with a high wage is not a bargain.
meta: Updated 13 November 2026 · FM27 released 10 November 2026 · This page gives the method and the live list sources instead of repeating fee estimates that age within days.
body:
A fixed list of “cheap players” is stale the week it is written. Fees move with the save, the database and the seller's mood, so this page does something more durable: it points at the maintainer lists that actually stay current, and gives the sum to run before you call anyone a bargain.

Where the live lists are

ListUse it forWhere
Cheap FM27 wonderkidsYoung players whose asking price is low relative to potentialsortitoutsi wonderkid list — the bargain section sits below the main table
Best free playersUnattached players, where the cost is wages and signing fees rather than a transfer feesortitoutsi free-player list
Expiring contractsPlayers you can approach for free at the end of a seasonsortitoutsi expiring-contract list
Bargain playersThe maintainer's own low-cost shortlistsortitoutsi bargain list

Those pages are updated by their maintainer, which is why they are worth more than a frozen table here. Read the column headings on each page before trusting a number: cost, value and wage are three different fields, and the gap between cost and value is usually the seller's premium for potential.

The sum to run before calling anyone cheap

  1. Fee — the asking price in your save, not the list estimate. They rarely match.
  2. Signing and agent fees — treat as a separate line, not as part of the fee.
  3. Wages over the seasons you expect to keep him. A £600k fee with a £74k wage is more expensive over three years than a £4m fee on £8k.
  4. Bonuses — appearance, goal and promotion clauses. Keep guaranteed instalments separate from conditional add-ons.
  5. Registration and eligibility — work permits, foreign-player limits and squad rules can stop a deal that the budget allows.
The wage-field trap: database profiles often show a wage number without stating the period. If the period is not written down, do not multiply it by 52 and call it an annual cost — confirm the unit in your own game first.

Two worked examples, and why they are dated

An earlier version of this page named Thomas Müller and Rui Araki with fee estimates read on 30 October 2026, during the Launch Preview. Those figures are left here only as an illustration of the method, not as current prices: the released database and the first post-launch updates can both move them, and this site will not present a five-week-old estimate as today's asking price.

  • Müller, the veteran case — a low headline fee with a high wage. The lesson is the wage line, not the fee.
  • Araki, the young case — a value figure far below the estimated cost. The lesson is that value and cost are different fields.

If you want their current numbers, open the player profile on the list site and read the same three columns — cost, wage, contract — that the method above uses.

Filters that find value in any save

  • Contracts expiring at the end of your first season, subject to the rules on when you may approach.
  • Transfer-listed and loan-listed players at clubs with surplus depth in your position.
  • Unattached players, with signing fees and wage demands included in the comparison.
  • Release clauses below the asking price, after confirming the clause applies to your club.
  • Young players at smaller clubs who will actually get minutes, rather than sit behind a starter.
